title: Certification readiness: rework keyboard flows, ARIA roles, and contrast tokens
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: prepare the design system for formal accessibility certification (VPAT) by auditing and remediating keyboard navigation patterns, ARIA usage, and color token contrast across buttons, tables, charts and data lists. Deliverables: updated token mappings, keyboard-first interaction spec, ARIA guidance doc for interactive visualizations, and a draft VPAT addendum for components modified in this cycle.
acceptance_criteria: Keyboard navigation implemented and documented for primary components (buttons, data tables, sortable headers, chart tooltips) with deterministic focus order
ARIA roles and attributes corrected or documented where semantic HTML is insufficient; pattern guidance added for screen-reader-friendly charts
All color tokens used in components meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast ratios (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text) or have approved exceptions documented
A draft VPAT section describing affected components is prepared and reviewed by legal/compliance
Design tokens and token aliases updated with migration notes; deprecation window documented
Automated visual/contrast tests added to the DS CI that flag token changes which reduce contrast below thresholds
tasks: Run full component audit: buttons, tables, paginators, charts, chart legends, and dropdowns
Decide keyboard strategy for compound components: roving tabindex vs native focus + aria-activedescendant
Create updated token palette and map token usages in component library
Prototype keyboard flows in Figma and user-test with keyboard-only personas
Update component docs with ARIA examples and recommended patterns
Author VPAT narrative for component changes and list remaining exceptions with mitigations
Open PRs: token changes, markup + attribute updates, and documentation updates
Add CI check: contrast-linter job and visual-diff gating on token diffs
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Initial audit completed for buttons and table components. Found 7 contrast token violations in compact table rows and 3 instances of missing aria-sort on sortable headers.

2025-02-17: Decision: use roving tabindex for composite widgets (menu/grid combos) where keyboard focus needs a single logical active item; preserve native focus for simple lists to retain browser semantics. Rationale: roving tabindex yields better single-focus management for virtualized grids used in Dedicated console, but increases markup complexity.
2025-02-22: Token refactor proposal posted in Confluence with migration plan and alias deprecation schedule (6 weeks). Avoid changing global semantic token names to minimize consumer churn.
2025-02-26: Figma prototypes for table keyboard interactions uploaded; design QA passed for focus indicators and focus order. Noted need to widen focus ring for high-contrast theme.

2025-03-02: Draft VPAT addendum created (section 'Interactive Components - Design System'); awaiting review from Compliance and PMs. Legal asked for explicit fallback behaviors for chart tooltips when JS is disabled.
review_feedback: PM (Evelyn Park): emphasize backward compatibility and communicate token deprecations with migration scripts
Engineering (Jinsoo Kim): requested examples for screen reader announcements during live chart updates; wants aria-live guidance
Accessibility consultant (external): flagged use of aria-hidden for decorative SVGs but recommended focusable wrappers for interactive chart elements
Compliance: asked to include owner contact and remediation timelines in VPAT draft
notes: Trade-offs: roving tabindex simplifies active-item management for virtualized grids but requires an explicit announcement strategy for screen readers; agreed to add aria-live region updates when selection changes
Contrast strategy: increase semantic token contrast for 'muted' text in tables rather than altering component spacing to avoid layout regressions in embedded consoles
Migration: provide codemods for token alias replacements and a clear deprecation schedule in release notes
